title: Escrowed, time-windowed pseudonymization for console analytics with legal-hold support
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a staged pseudonymization pipeline for console analytics events that separates derivable analytics data from an encrypted escrow of raw PII. The pipeline will enforce time-windowed retention policies, support legal-hold exemptions, and provide provable deletion manifests for audits. This ticket covers design, implementation of tokenization/escrow primitives, deletion orchestration, and observability hooks.
background: Current analytics ingestion stores event payloads with fields that may contain PII (email, username, IP). We already have scrubbing jobs but lack a robust escrow + revocable-pseudonymization flow that: 1) enables analytics use-cases (joins and counts) without exposing raw PII, 2) retains the ability to satisfy legal-hold or support requests against a small encrypted escrow, and 3) produces provable deletion manifests when retention windows expire. Past tickets improved scrubbing; this ticket unifies escrowed storage and staged erasure across pipelines.
goals: Deliver per-tenant deterministic pseudonymization scheme compatible with analytics joins and aggregations
Store raw, minimally-indexed PII in an encrypted escrow vault with HSM-wrapped keys and limited access policies
Support legal-hold flags that exempt specific customer records from automated deletion
Provide deletion manifests and audit logs proving removal from both analytics tables and escrow within SLA
Add metrics and traces to measure pseudonymization coverage, escrow hits, deletion latency, and access requests
proposed_solution: On ingest, run a lightweight schema-aware tokenizer that replaces PII fields with deterministic tokens derived from: HMAC_SHA256(PII + tenant_salt + field_tag) truncated to 64 bits. Persist tokens in analytics stores. Simultaneously, write an encrypted escrow record containing minimal raw PII, an escrow_id (UUID), tenant_id, field_tag, created_at, legal_hold boolean, and a tombstone flag. Escrow encryption uses envelope encryption: data encrypted with a per-tenant data key, which is wrapped by the service master key stored in KMS/HSM. Access to escrowed raw data requires an additional approval workflow and ephemeral unwrapping tokens (auditable). Retention engine runs nightly to: 1) mark expired records in analytics for deletion, 2) for non-legal-hold escrow records, trigger a staged erasure that rotates/obliterates the per-tenant key and sets tombstone metadata, and 3) emit a signed deletion manifest (SHA256 list) to the compliance topic and S3 archive for audits. Legal-hold records are moved to an isolated vault and excluded from rotation until release. To allow safe re-identification for specific support workflows, implement an unblinding flow that requires: requestor identity, justification, short-lived HSM attest, and an entry in the audit log.
tasks: Design token format and per-tenant salt scheme (security review)
Implement tokenizer library in ingestion service with schema mapping
Provision escrow store (encrypted DynamoDB or Postgres schema) and KMS key policies
Build escrow write/read API with strict RBAC and request auditing
Implement nightly retention/orchestrator job with staged erasure steps
Add legal-hold flag support and isolated vaulting path
Create deletion manifest generator and signed manifest publisher
Integrate observability: metrics, traces, alerting, and dashboards
End-to-end tests, property tests, and compliance QA runbook
Prepare rollout canary and migration plan for existing events
acceptance_criteria: New ingestion replaces PII fields with deterministic tokens for 95% of schema-mapped events in canary
Escrow contains encrypted raw values accessible only via audited APIs and HSM-wrapped keys
Nightly retention job deletes analytics tokens and rotates keys for non-legal-hold data within SLA (max 48h from retention expiry)
Deletion manifests are verifiable (signed) and contain checksums proving removal of escrow entries
Unblinding flow requires RBAC approval and leaves immutable audit entry; no unblinding may occur without proper justification
Dashboards show pseudonymization coverage and deletion latencies; alerts fire if retention lag > 24h
rollout_plan: Phase 1: implement tokenizer + escrow APIs and run in shadow mode for 2 weeks; Phase 2: pilot for 5% of tenant traffic with read-only escrow verification; Phase 3: enable tokenization for all non-sensitive event types and begin retention enforcement for pilot tenants; Phase 4: full rollout with legal-hold migrations and compliance QA. At each phase we will run smoke checks against query results and compare cardinalities to pre-tokenization baselines.
risks: Deterministic tokens enable cross-tenant linking if tenant_salt is leaked — mitigated by per-tenant salt rotation and strict key management
Escrow store becomes a high-value target — mitigated with HSM wrapping, minimal indexing, and RBAC gating
Key rotation complexity could lead to accidental data loss — mitigated with rehearsal runs and retained復鍵 (recovery) window
Analytics joins may change cardinality after tokenization — mitigated by canary comparisons and compensating aggregation adjustments
